title: Microsoft made $10bn from OpenAI last quarter, 11% of its revenue
content:
Microsoft recorded $10bn of revenue from its business with OpenAI in the three months to September, about 11% of its total revenue. Microsoft disclosed the amount in its quarterly filing on Wednesday, the day it reported its results.
It is the first time Microsoft has given a quarterly figure for the arrangement, Todd Bishop reported for GeekWire. Rebecca Bellan also reported the figure for TechCrunch.
“For the three months ended September 30, 2026, we recorded revenue from commercial arrangements with OpenAI, inclusive of revenue-sharing payments, of $10.0 billion,” the filing says.
The filing does not split that between revenue sharing and OpenAI’s spending on Azure, Microsoft’s cloud.
Bigger than Xbox
In the 12 months to June, Microsoft recorded $24.1bn from OpenAI, both outlets reported. That is about $6bn a quarter on average. Last quarter’s OpenAI revenue of $10bn was more than Xbox brought in ($5.4bn) and more than search and advertising ($6.6bn), GeekWire reported.
OpenAI owed Microsoft $7.2bn at the end of September, the filing shows, up from $6.0bn in June. Microsoft owns about 24% of OpenAI, and has paid $12.0bn of the $13.0bn it committed to invest.
That stake was about 25% in June and about 27% after OpenAI’s restructuring in October 2025, TechCrunch reported. Microsoft did not say what caused the dilution. Microsoft must disclose the business because OpenAI counts as a related party under accounting rules, GeekWire reported.
Looser ties
The two companies have loosened their partnership, both outlets reported. In October 2025, Microsoft gave up its right of first refusal to supply OpenAI’s computing capacity. OpenAI committed to buy another $250bn of Azure services. An April 2026 agreement gave OpenAI broader freedom to use other cloud providers, and OpenAI recently brought its models to rival Google Cloud.
OpenAI will keep sharing revenue with Microsoft through 2030, subject to a cap, TechCrunch reported. It noted earlier reports that OpenAI shares 20% of its revenue, a figure neither company has confirmed.
On the earnings call, Bernstein analyst Mark Moerdler asked where Azure’s AI growth was coming from. Chief executive Satya Nadella did not mention OpenAI, GeekWire reported. He said he did not want Azure’s AI business to depend on a few big customers.
Relying on “four customers who buy a lot of capacity from you” for a few quarters of growth is “not a business as far as I’m concerned”, Nadella said, according to GeekWire.
In a post on X after the call, Nadella wrote that Azure’s growth was broad-based across large and small businesses.
4/ When it comes to infrastructure, we have a fungible fleet that allows us to dynamically allocate capacity to the highest value opportunities across compute, data, Foundry, and Copilot.
We are bringing capacity online faster, and getting more from the infrastructure we already have.
Azure growth was broad-based across enterprise and SMB, spanning both core cloud services and AI infra.
I have never been more confident in the opportunity ahead of us.
Satya Nadella (@satyanadella) October 28, 2026
Microsoft also widened a warning in the filing about its reliance on outside AI model makers, GeekWire reported. It says Microsoft has “limited visibility into or control over” how those models are designed, trained, secured and tested. Some of those partners are also significant Azure customers, it adds.
Spending forecast trimmed
Chief financial officer Amy Hood cut Microsoft’s 2026 capital spending forecast to $170bn, from $175bn, Ashley Stewart reported for Business Insider. Hood said some “GPU-as-a-Service contracts” with outside capacity providers had slipped to the second half of the fiscal year.
Capital spending, including finance leases, was $45.2bn in the quarter, Jordan Novet reported for CNBC. That was below Microsoft’s own $50bn projection, according to Reuters. The cash part, spending on property and equipment, was $39.4bn, the filing shows.
Hood said spending would top $50bn in the current quarter, Brody Ford and Matt Day reported for Bloomberg. Investor relations chief Jonathan Neilson put the shortfall down to delays rather than any change in spending plans, Reuters reported.
Its headcount fell 2% in the quarter, according to Business Insider, which cited company slides. This week Microsoft offered buyouts to 60,000 employees.

report.summary: 微软单季从OpenAI获100亿美元收入，占总营收11%
report.background: 微软与OpenAI自2019年起深度绑定，累计承诺投资130亿美元、持股约24%，并通过Azure独家承载其算力、共享收入。随着OpenAI体量暴涨，这笔关联交易已成为微软财报中的重要变量，按会计准则必须披露。与此同时，双方关系正在松动：2025年10月微软放弃算力优先供应权，OpenAI承诺追加2500亿美元Azure采购；2026年4月协议进一步允许OpenAI使用其他云厂商，其模型近期也上架了竞争对手Google Cloud。
key_points: 微软首次单独披露OpenAI相关季度收入：截至9月底的三个月入账100亿美元，约占其总营收的11%，此前只公布年度数字。
OpenAI业务已超过Xbox（54亿美元）和搜索广告（66亿美元），成为微软内部举足轻重的收入来源，过去12个月累计贡献241亿美元。
OpenAI同期欠微软72亿美元，高于6月的60亿美元；微软已支付130亿投资承诺中的120亿，持股因重组稀释至约24%。
关系由“独家”转向“多云”：OpenAI可接其他云厂商，收入分成延续到2030年但设有上限，据传比例为20%（双方均未确认）。
CEO纳德拉强调Azure的AI增长要广泛分布，不能依赖“四五个大客户”；CFO将2026年资本开支预期从1750亿下调至1700亿美元，季度资本开支452亿低于原计划。
report.impact: 对AI行业，这标志着“云厂商+模型公司”的绑定模式进入重新定价期，独家算力换股权的旧结构正被多云采购取代。对开发者，OpenAI模型将更容易出现在AWS、Google Cloud等平台，选型更自由、议价空间更大，但微软对模型“设计、训练、安全缺乏可见性”的风险提示也意味着服务条款可能更谨慎。对普通用户，Copilot等产品的成本结构会随算力采购与多云策略变化，短期功能迭代加快，长期订阅价格存在上行压力。微软放缓资本开支与裁员买断，也暗示AI基建从“军备竞赛”转向效率优先。
report.tools: 想跟进可关注 Azure AI Foundry 与 Copilot Studio 了解微软侧落地；OpenAI 官方 API 与 Playground 观察模型更新。开发者若想避免单一供应商锁定，可上手开源路由层 LiteLLM、OpenRouter，以及 vLLM、SGLang 等自托管推理框架，配合多云部署做成本与可用性对比。
